Brand Overview

What is Root Revive? Lumin Root Revive is a hair growth supplement capsule formulated specifically for Black women. It targets chronic scalp inflammation — the root cause of thinning edges, crown loss, and alopecia — from the inside out. 17 clinically proven ingredients including Black Seed Extract, Bamboo Extract, Boswellia, Saw Palmetto, Iron, Vitamin D, and Copper. 2 capsules a day. Made by Black women, for Black women. 200,000+ customers.
ProductRoot Revive Hair Growth Capsules
Key ClaimTargets scalp inflammation from within — not a topical, not an oil
Key DifferentiatorOnly hair supplement built specifically for Black women's biology
Dosage2 capsules per day
Guarantee90-day money back guarantee
Current Offer60% off + free shipping
Social Proof200,000+ Black women
02

Target Audience — Know Her

This is critical for every editing decision you make. Every cut, every B-roll choice, every caption must speak to this woman specifically. If it could be for anyone — it's for no one.

Who She Is

Black women, ages 35–64, USA. Teachers, nurses, corporate professionals. She is battle-tested, savvy, and her tolerance for BS is extremely low. She has tried everything.

Her Pain

Thinning edges, traction alopecia, CCCA, menopausal hair loss. She hides under wigs and scarves. She avoids mirrors, photos, and events. She has given up.

What She's Tried

Castor oil. Biotin. Nutrafol ($80/mo). Viviscal. $200 salon treatments. None of it worked because none of it was made for her.

How She Talks

"My roof top is missing." "I've been wearing wigs since 2010." "I thought it was just genetics." "I almost didn't try this." "I just live with it."

Top Converting Age Bracket 45–54 is the highest volume converter. 55–64 is a strong second. Never cast or feature anyone who looks under 40. This is non-negotiable.
03

Hair Visual Guide — Pain vs Results

Read this before choosing any B-roll or before/after footage. You need to know exactly what "thinning edges" and "crown loss" look like — and what the result hair should look like. Wrong footage kills trust instantly.

THE PAIN — What Her Hair Looks Like BEFORE Root Revive

Pain Area #1
Thinning Edges
The hairline along the forehead and temples is sparse or completely bare. You can see scalp where hair should be. Often caused by tight braids, weaves, and traction over years. This is the #1 pain point for our audience.
Pain Area #2
Thinning Crown / "Roof Top"
The top/centre of the head is see-through — you can see straight through to the scalp. Often called "my roof top is missing" in comments. Looks like a widening part or bald patch at the top. Extremely common in menopausal women.
Pain Area #3
Overall Thinning / Shedding
Hair overall looks thin, flat, and lifeless. Ponytail is see-through. Hair in drain after every wash. Pillow covered in shed hair in the morning. She hides it under wigs, scarves, and hats.

THE RESULT — What Her Hair Looks Like AFTER Root Revive

Result #1 — Day 30
Baby Hairs at Edges
Tiny new hairs appearing along the hairline. Soft, fine, visible. The first sign that follicles are waking up. This is the emotional moment — she can't believe it. Show this in extreme close-up.
Result #2 — Day 60
Crown Filling In
The see-through area at the top is noticeably thicker. The part looks narrower. New growth is visible across the crown. She's standing in front of the mirror with a completely different expression.
Result #3 — Day 90-120
Full Edges / Crown Restored
Edges are back. Crown is full. She's walking out without a wig for the first time in years. Hair looks thick, healthy, and full of life. This is the crown she was born with.

BEFORE vs AFTER — What Good Footage Looks Like

✗ Before — Use This Footage

  • Sparse, thin hairline along forehead
  • Visible scalp at temples
  • See-through part at crown
  • Thin, flat, lifeless overall
  • Hair pulled back revealing bare edges
  • Natural hair — NO WIG SHOTS
→

✓ After — Use This Footage

  • Baby hairs visible along hairline
  • Full, defined edges
  • Thick crown — no scalp visible
  • Hair looks full and healthy
  • Emotional reaction — touching edges
  • Natural hair — NO WIG SHOTS
⚠️ NEVER use wig shots in before/after comparisons. If the "before" shows a wig or the "after" shows a wig — cut it immediately. Real customers called this out in comments and it destroys trust. Always use natural hair footage only.
04

Editing Guidelines — Technical Standards

SAFE ZONE — Where to Place All Text & Graphics

Everything important must stay inside the safe zone. Facebook, Instagram, and TikTok all crop the edges of 9:16 videos. UI elements (like/comment buttons, profile info, captions) cover the bottom and sides. Anything outside the safe zone will be hidden or cut off.
Canvas Size
Full frame: 1080 x 1920px
Safe zone: 960 x 1560px
Left/right margin: 60px each side
Top margin: 180px from top
Bottom margin: 180px from bottom
Platform UI Zones to Avoid
Top 150px → profile info / ad label
Bottom 250px → like/comment/share buttons
Right edge 80px → action bar icons
Keep all captions above bottom 300px
Keep hook text in middle 60% of frame
✓ SAFE ZONE
All text here
Frame Zones
Danger zone — UI covers this area
Right edge — action bar buttons here
Safe zone — all text, captions, graphics
Hook text: centre of frame, middle third
Captions: lower third, above 300px from bottom
Product name/logo: upper safe zone only

CAPTIONS — Style & Placement

SettingSpecification
FontBold sans-serif — Arial Bold, Montserrat Bold, or similar. Never script or decorative fonts.
ColourWhite text (#FFFFFF) with black stroke/shadow. Never yellow, red, or coloured — always white.
Stroke3–5px black outline OR drop shadow. Must be readable on any background.
Size60–72px at 1080x1920. Never smaller — she may be watching on a small phone screen.
PositionLower third — between 55% and 80% down the frame. Never in the bottom 300px (UI zone).
StyleBurned in — not as a separate subtitle track. Every single word must be covered.
TimingSync exactly to speech. No delay. No early pop. Captions should feel natural, not distracting.
EmphasisKey words can be capitalised (e.g. "HEAL it", "Baby HAIRS") — use sparingly for impact.

HOOK TEXT OVERLAYS — Style Guide

Hooks have NO voice over — text overlay does all the work. The hook text is the first thing she reads. It needs to stop the scroll in under 2 seconds.
SettingSpecification
FontHeavy/Black weight — Montserrat Black, Impact, or Arial Black. Bold and impossible to miss.
ColourWhite with thick black stroke OR black text on white semi-transparent pill/box.
Size80–100px. Large. Fill the middle of the frame. It should feel like a poster.
PositionVertical centre of frame — in the middle 40% of the screen height.
AnimationSimple fade in or word-by-word pop. No spinning, bouncing, or distracting transitions.
DurationHold for 3–4 seconds minimum so she can read it fully before the creator appears.
Line breaksBreak at natural pauses. Max 5–6 words per line. Never let text run edge to edge.

COLOUR GRADING — Look & Feel

SettingDirection
Overall toneWarm and natural. Not cold, not clinical. This is a personal, emotional brand.
Skin tonesCRITICAL — preserve accurate dark skin tones. Never over-expose or bleach. Never add cool blue tones that wash out melanin. Warm up if needed.
BrightnessSlightly warm and bright. Not dark or moody. She needs to feel hopeful watching this.
SaturationNatural — do not over-saturate. Avoid neon or Instagram-filter looks.
Pain sectionsSlightly desaturated / cooler tone to match the emotional low point.
Results sectionsWarmer, brighter — lift the grade when results appear. She should feel the transformation.

TRANSITIONS & CUTS

SituationWhat to Use
Default cutHard cut only. Clean and fast. No cross dissolves between normal clips.
Between sectionsHard cut or very fast dip (2–4 frames max). Never a slow fade.
Before/After revealSimple hard cut or 2-frame flash white. The contrast does the work — no need for fancy transitions.
Emotional momentsSlow down the pacing with slightly longer holds — don't cut away too fast. Let it breathe.
Never useWipes, spins, glitch effects, zoom punches on every cut, star wipes. Keep it clean and native-feeling.

MUSIC & AUDIO

SettingDirection
Music volume10–15% under voice. Never louder than the creator speaking. She must hear every word.
Hook sectionMusic can be slightly louder (20–25%) since there is no voice over on hooks.
Music styleWarm, soulful, understated. No EDM, no trap, no jarring beats. Think: soft R&B, gospel undertone, emotional indie.
Voice clarityCreator audio must be clean. Apply light noise reduction if needed. No echo, no reverb.
Music fadeFade out music under CTA — let the final offer land in near-silence for impact.

06

Editing Rules — Non-Negotiable

1
No wig shots in before/afters
Natural hair only. If before or after shows a wig — cut it. This destroys trust instantly and was called out directly in comments.
2
Hook must be tight — no dead air in first 3 seconds
No fade in. No slow zoom. No music swell before the hook. Cut straight to the creator or visual. Every second counts.
3
Social proof clips before the story — not after
60% of viewers gone by 0:15 seconds. Move UGC proof clips to 0:05–0:15. Skeptics need results before they invest in the story.
4
Creators must visually appear 45–64
Converting demographic is 45–64 Black women. If a creator looks under 40 — do not use them as the main face.
5
Captions on every word — always
85% of social media is watched on mute. Every word must be captioned. White text, dark shadow/outline. No coloured captions.
6
Aspect ratio 9:16 always — 1080x1920px
All ads formatted for mobile feed. Never deliver 16:9 or 1:1 unless brief explicitly says so.
7
Hook text overlays — no voice over on hooks
All 3 hooks in every batch are text overlay ONLY. No VO. Creator speaking begins at Section 1.
8
Results timeline must appear as on-screen text
Day 30 / Day 60 / Day 90 / Day 120 must appear as text when spoken. Helps muted viewers follow the transformation.
9
Product bottle clearly visible for minimum 3 seconds
Root Revive bottle shown clearly — label readable. Do not rush past it. This is brand recall.
10
Deliver 3 versions — one per hook
Every batch = 3 separate files. Naming: Hook1_[BatchName]_[Date], Hook2_[BatchName]_[Date], Hook3_[BatchName]_[Date].
07

Do's & Don'ts

✓ Always Do

  • Cut tight — no dead air anywhere
  • Use warm, natural lighting on creators
  • Show scalp/hairline B-rolls in close up
  • Caption every single word
  • Keep UGC clips raw and authentic
  • Show the bottle clearly at reveal
  • Match music energy to emotional arc
  • Deliver 3 hook versions per batch
  • Use creators who look 45–64
  • Follow the editing brief exactly

✗ Never Do

  • Use wig shots in before/afters
  • Add dead air or slow fades at start
  • Use creators who look under 40
  • Put social proof only at the end
  • Deliver in 16:9 format
  • Use coloured or hard to read captions
  • Rush past the product bottle shot
  • Add voice over to hook sections
  • Use generic stock footage
  • Deliver only one hook version

B-Roll Guide

B-Roll Footage Folder All approved B-roll footage is here: https://f.io/zOYqRwfa — always pull from this folder first before sourcing elsewhere.
SectionB-Roll Direction
Hook (text overlay)Extreme close-up of thinning edges / patchy crown / sparse hairline. No creator face. Just the hair showing the problem.
Pain / StruggleCreator talking to camera, slightly leaned in. Warm backdrop — bathroom, bedroom, natural lighting. Authentic, not overly produced.
Failed ProductsCastor oil bottle, biotin gummies, supplements — shown and dismissed. Creator counting on fingers.
Product RevealCreator holds Root Revive bottle close to camera. Slow reveal. Label clearly visible. Confident energy.
Results TimelineBefore/after hair shots — natural hair ONLY, no wigs. Close-up of edges, crown, hairline. Genuine emotional reaction.
Social Proof ClipsUGC style — different Black women, ages 35–60, talking to camera. 3–4 seconds each. Raw and real.
CTACreator holds bottle, smiles directly at camera. Points warmly at lens. Genuine and direct.
